title: The sky will split open.
subtitle: The ceiling of the world cracks
then: Ibn Kathir explains it simply: {trap}it splits{/trap}, citing 73:18. The Prophet ﷺ named this surah among those to read to {idea}see the Day of Resurrection as if with your own eyes{/idea}, and suggested it to Muadh as a fitting recitation for prayer.
now: You look up at a clear blue sky on your lunch break, and it looks like it could never break. {idea}It will.{/idea} Short surahs like this one are a gift for your next prayer, easy to recite and full of weight.
old: The sky above me is the most unchanging thing there is.
new: Even the sky will split. This surah helps me picture that Day.
try: Recite this surah in one of your prayers today, or listen to it once.

title: The planets and stars will drop.
subtitle: What held its place, falling
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}fallen.{/trap} After the sky splits, the lights inside it fall. {idea}The same order that held them all this time is lifted.{/idea} This echoes 81:2, a surah from about the same period.
now: You stand on a dark beach on holiday, the sky crowded with stars, and feel tiny. {idea}They hang there because Allah holds them.{/idea} So does every part of your day.
new: Every star stays in place only because Allah holds it there.
try: Say subhanAllah three times the next time you look at the night sky.

title: The seas burst into each other.
subtitle: Boundaries that held, broken
then: Ibn Abbas said {trap}Allah will cause some of it to burst forth over other parts.{/trap} Al-Hasan added that its water will go away. Qatadah said {idea}its fresh water will mix with its salt water.{/idea}
now: You keep your work self and your private self in separate boxes, like fresh and salt water. {idea}On that Day the walls come down.{/idea} The goal is to be one person all the way through.
old: I can keep different parts of my life sealed off from each other.
new: One day all walls break. Better to be the same person everywhere now.
try: Notice one place where your private and public self differ, and close the gap a little.

title: Graves are turned over and emptied.
subtitle: Those inside come out
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}searched.{/idea} As-Suddi said {reward}they will be moved and those who are in them will come out.{/reward} The cosmic scenes now turn to people.
now: You drive past the cemetery on your way to work every day without a thought. {idea}Every grave there will open.{/idea} Including the one that will one day be yours.
old: Once someone is buried, their story is over.
new: Every grave will open, and every story continues.
try: Make dua today for the people buried in the nearest cemetery to you.

title: Each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind.
subtitle: Deeds done and deeds neglected
then: Ibn Kathir says simply {idea}when this happens, then this will occur.{/idea} After the sky, stars, seas and graves, {reward}each person knows what they sent forward and what they left behind.{/reward}
now: The donation you meant to make, the visit to your aunt you kept postponing, the course of Quran you never started. {trap}Those sit on the left-behind list.{/trap} You still have time to move some across.
old: As long as I avoid bad things, I am fine.
new: The good I kept putting off will also be shown to me.
try: Do one good thing today that you have postponed for more than a month.

title: What fooled you about your Generous Lord?
subtitle: Generosity is not permission

row.title: He is kind, so it is fine
He is kind, so shame on me

then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}this is a threat, not an attempt to get a reply.{/trap} It means: O son of Adam, what deceived you about your Lord, {idea}the Most Great, so that you went forth disobeying Him?{/idea} Allah will ask on the Day: what deceived you concerning Me?
now: You skip a prayer and tell yourself Allah is forgiving, He will understand. {idea}His generosity is real.{/idea} The verse asks whether you are using it as a reason to come closer, or an excuse to stay away.
old: Allah is so generous, my slips do not really matter.
new: Because Allah is so generous, I should be ashamed to meet Him carelessly.
try: When you catch yourself saying Allah will understand today, take that as a cue to do the deed instead.

title: He made you, shaped you, balanced you.
subtitle: Three gifts in your own body
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}He made you complete, straight, and perfectly balanced.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ placed a finger on spit in his palm and related Allah's words: I made you from something like this, then you gathered wealth and withheld it, {trap}until at death you say: now I will give charity.{/trap}
now: You stand at the mirror and only see what you want to change. {reward}Two working hands, eyes that read this.{/reward} The hadith adds one more warning: do not wait until the last breath to be generous.
old: My body is just how it happens to be, with flaws I dislike.
new: Allah shaped and balanced me on purpose, and I can give back with it now.
try: Give some charity today, any amount, while it is easy.

title: In whatever form He chose, He put you together.
subtitle: Your face, chosen by Allah
then: Mujahid said it means {idea}in which resemblance: the father, the mother, the paternal uncle, or the maternal uncle.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites a man who came to the Prophet ﷺ worried that his child did not look like him, and was told {reward}it is probably an inherited strain.{/reward}
now: At family gatherings someone always says: he has his grandfather's nose. {idea}That nose was chosen.{/idea} Your face is not an accident to be ashamed of, and neither is anyone else's.
old: How I look is just luck, good or bad.
new: Allah chose the form He assembled me in, and that is enough.
try: Stop yourself from one comment about your own looks, or someone else's, today.

title: The real reason: you deny the reckoning.
subtitle: The root under careless living
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}you are only compelled to oppose the Most Generous{/trap} because you reject in your hearts {idea}the Hereafter, the recompense and the reckoning.{/idea} The question in verse 6 now gets its answer.
now: You would never cheat on an exam if you knew the invigilator was watching. {idea}The cheating starts when you stop believing anyone will check.{/idea} The verse puts the finger on that quiet doubt.
old: I believe in the Day, but it does not affect much of what I do.
new: The less real the reckoning feels, the more careless I become.
try: Before one decision today, ask: how will this look on the Day?

title: There are guardians over you.
subtitle: You are never unattended
then: Right after naming the denial of the Day, Allah answers it: {idea}indeed there are noble guardian angels over you.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says, {trap}so do not meet them with evil deeds.{/trap}
now: You are alone in the car at midnight, or in a hotel room on a work trip. {idea}You are not actually alone.{/idea} That can be a comfort as much as a check.
old: When I am by myself, no one sees what I do.
new: Allah's appointed guardians are with me, even in empty rooms.
try: In your next moment alone today, do one small good thing for your guardians to write.

title: Noble writers, recording.
subtitle: The dignity of who writes your record
then: Ibn Kathir describes them as {reward}noble guardian angels{/reward} who {idea}write down all that you do.{/idea} The surah introduction calls them trustworthy writers preparing a complete record.
now: Imagine someone you deeply respect sitting beside you at your desk all day. {reward}You would choose your words differently.{/reward} The ones beside you are nobler than any person you know.
new: Noble companions are writing, and I can give them something good to write.
try: Say one kind sentence today that you would be glad to have written down.

title: They know whatever you do.
subtitle: Nothing slips past the record
then: Ibn Kathir reads verses 10 to 12 together: there are guardian angels over you, {idea}they write down all that you do.{/idea} {reward}The record is complete{/reward}, and it is being prepared now, as the surah introduction says.
now: The extra minute of patience with a slow cashier. The snide reply you typed and deleted. {idea}All of it is known.{/idea} That means no good thing you do is ever wasted.
old: Small things I do are not worth recording.
new: Everything I do is known, so every small good counts.
try: Do one tiny good deed today on purpose, knowing it will be written.

title: The righteous will be in delight.
subtitle: Where the record of the obedient leads

row.title: the obedient
sub: did not meet Him with sin

then: After the noble writers, the surah shows where the record leads. Ibn Kathir says the righteous are {idea}those who obeyed Allah and did not meet Him with disobedience.{/idea} {reward}Delight is what awaits them.{/reward}
now: You picture the righteous as people with perfect beards and perfect prayer streaks. {idea}The tafsir says the obedient.{/idea} Someone who keeps turning back to Allah after slipping is walking that road.
old: The righteous are a different kind of person from me.
new: The righteous are those who obey Allah, and I can be one of them.
try: Choose one act of obedience you find hard and do it once today, for Allah.

title: And the wicked will be in the Fire.
subtitle: The other end of the record
then: The verse sits directly opposite the one before it. Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}mentions that the evildoers will be in Hell{/trap}, after naming the delight of the obedient. {idea}Two endings, written side by side, so no one can claim they were not told.{/idea}
now: You read two paths in a single breath, one bright and one dark. {idea}You are still standing at the fork.{/idea} Every ordinary choice today is a step toward one of them.
old: Hell is about other, really bad people.
new: Both endings are real, and my own deeds are walking me toward one.
try: Leave one sin today that you know you have been holding on to.

title: They enter it on the Day of Recompense.
subtitle: The Day when deeds are paid back
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Day of ad-Din as {idea}the Day of Reckoning, Recompense, and Judgement.{/idea} The same word appeared in verse 9: {trap}you deny ad-Din.{/trap} Those who denied that Day meet it.
now: You say maliki yawm ad-din in every rakah, often on autopilot. {idea}This is that Day.{/idea} Next time, slow down on those words.
old: Payback for what I do is a vague, distant idea.
new: There is a Day set for recompense, and I name it in every prayer.
try: In your next prayer, pause on maliki yawm ad-din and think of its meaning.

title: No absence from it, not even an hour.
subtitle: No break, no way out
then: Ibn Kathir explains {trap}they will not be absent for even one hour from the torment{/trap}, with no rest and no lightening. {idea}The verse is said while doors are still open{/idea}, to people who could still turn.
now: You get a final notice on a bill and still have a week to pay. {idea}This is that week.{/idea} The verse is serious so that you use the time you have, not so you despair.
old: There will always be another chance to fix things.
new: The chances are now. Allah warns me so I use them.
try: Ask Allah's forgiveness 100 times today, in any free moments.

title: Do you even know what that Day is?
subtitle: A question that magnifies
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is a magnification of the affair of the Day of Judgement.{/idea} After describing both destinations, Allah pauses to ask: {reward}what will make you know what it is?{/reward}
now: You hear a talk about the Day and think: yes, I know all this. {idea}The verse says you do not, not really.{/idea} Some truths need to be felt again, not just known.
old: I already know everything there is about the Day of Judgement.
new: The Day is bigger than anything I have pictured.
try: Sit quietly for two minutes today and honestly imagine standing before Allah.

title: Again: do you know what that Day is?
subtitle: The question asked twice
then: Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah affirms it by saying again{/idea} the same question, and then {reward}explains it{/reward} in the next verse. The repetition holds the listener still before the answer comes.
now: Your parent says your name twice when something really matters. You look up from your phone. {idea}This is that second calling of your name.{/idea}
old: Hearing the same reminder twice is just repetition.
new: When Allah repeats a question, He wants me to stop and listen.
try: Read verses 17 and 18 aloud slowly, and pause before reading 19.

title: No soul can help another. The command is Allah's.
subtitle: The answer to the question
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}no one will be able to benefit anyone else{/trap}, unless Allah permits. The Prophet ﷺ told his own clan: save yourselves from the Fire. Qatadah said, {idea}the Decision is Allah's today, but on that Day no one will dispute Him.{/idea}
now: You count on your parents' prayers, your sheikh's dua, your family's good name. {idea}Those are blessings, but you will stand alone.{/idea} The command is Allah's now too, so turn to Him now.
old: Someone good in my family will be able to help me then.
new: Only Allah decides that Day, and He already decides today, so I turn to Him now.
try: Make one dua today directly to Allah, without asking anyone else to pray for you first.
